title: A scoped 'intent sync --to-store ID' refuses on view-skew belonging to a DIFFERENT thread -- but only when the named thread has work to write, so the estate-wide block is invisible to every node except the one with real work, whose only unblocking move is to discard another node's edit
body:
**Two halves, one shape: an instrument answering from a narrower or older view than the question, with nothing marking the difference.**

## 1. `intent sync --to-store <ID>` refuses on findings belonging to a DIFFERENT thread, but only when the named thread has something to write

Lamplight's `dc` node ran `intent sync --to-store ST0359`, scoped to its own thread:

```
error: could not read the committed canon
  caused by: residue: intent/st/ST0356/info.md -- view-skew --
  the preamble (authored, but not carried) was edited by hand and does not round-trip
error: refused 2 finding(s) -- view-skew: 2
```

**ST0356 is a different thread, owned by a different node.** dc could not reconcile its own two attachments because somebody else's thread had a hand-edited preamble.

**The discriminating variable is whether the named thread has a difference to write, and that is the part worth fixing.** `intent sync --to-store ST0358` on a thread with nothing to write SUCCEEDS in the same repository in the same minute:

```
note: no thread the store already holds differs on disk, so this restore overwrites nothing
ok: store rewritten from the canon extract, 1 thread(s)
```

So the whole-canon check is coupled to having work to do. **A node with nothing to sync never learns the estate is blocked; only the node with real work hits the wall** -- and it hits it over a thread it does not own, cannot assess, and should not edit. The remedy the tool offers for the blocking finding is `intent sync --to-disk`, which DISCARDS the hand edit, so the blocked node's only unblocking move is to destroy another node's uncommitted work.

**ONE CAUSE PROPOSED AND RULED OUT, recorded because a wrong cause in an issue is worse than no cause.** The gate reads back only `## Objective` and `## Context`, and `ST0356/info.md` carries a seven-line block-quote preamble between the title and `## Objective` -- so "a preamble cannot round-trip" was the obvious hypothesis. **It is refuted.** Exactly two of the 22 on-disk `info.md` files in that estate carry a block quote before `## Objective`: ST0290 and ST0356. **ST0290 produced no view-skew finding at any point, and both refusals named only `ST0356/info.md`.** So a preamble sits happily in a file the gate is content with, and the cause is narrower -- most plausibly the specific prose under edit, consistent with the correction having had to be written into store and extract together by hand. This issue does not claim to know it.

## 2. The reconcile advice routes through a store whose staleness the same tool separately reports

In one `intent doctor` run, on the same estate, in the same minute:

```
residue: intent/.cache/intent.db -- model-inconsistent -- the runtime store does not
match a rebuild from committed canon -- commands are answering from the store and will
report the stale model until it is refreshed
```

and, computed from that same store, **zero `view-skew` findings** -- while `intent sync`, the one instrument here that does NOT read the runtime store (its error is literally `could not read the committed canon`), still refuses on two of them.

**So a node following the tool's own advice gets a green from the stale model and concludes it is fixed.** This is not hypothetical: it happened twice within an hour in that estate, once to the reporting node, which named the staleness caveat and then verified against `doctor` in the same message.

**A related hazard in the remedy text itself.** `doctor` offers deleting `intent/.cache/` on the grounds that the store is derived. **On that estate it was not derived** -- prose had been written into the store by hand, because no CLI verb writes it -- so a rebuild could have discarded a correction that had just been made. The remedy is correct about the general case and wrong about the instance, which is the shape that gets followed.

## What is wanted

**Report the finding's OWNER, and do not refuse a scoped command on a thread outside its scope** -- or, if a whole-canon read is genuinely required before any write, apply it consistently rather than only when there is work to do, so the blockage is visible to everyone and not just to whoever tried first.

**And make any check that answers from the runtime store say so when the store is known stale.** A green computed from a model the same run has flagged as out of date should not be printed as a green.

Reported by Lamplight's `vc` node; found and reproduced by Lamplight's `dc`. The `reporter` field in this register reads `Matthew Sinclair` on every row regardless of origin.
